shortlist.raw_text: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. We introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination, instantiated through ten task-specific metrics on a 0-100 scale. Evaluating 37 distinct models across 300 test cases, we find that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency. In particular, request execution remains challenging: the highest task-specific scores are 36.90 for Following among seven avatar-performance models, 25.93 for Following in text-conditioned world generation, and 15.00 for Edit Success among three reported reference-editing models. These findings identify reliable request execution under timing and preservation constraints as a central challenge for advancing omni-modal real-time interactive systems. The leaderboard is available at https://streameval.ai

shortlist.raw_text: Despite substantial progress in Deep Search agents, their ability to conduct end-to-end research in real-world open Web environments remains insufficiently evaluated. Unlike static retrieval settings, information on the real-world Web is distributed across diverse sources, modalities, and heterogeneous formats, often involving complex interaction mechanisms that require agents to autonomously search for, access, and integrate relevant evidence during execution. To address this gap, we introduce the OpenDS task, designed to evaluate agents' ability to perform multi-step deep search in the live, open Web. This task requires agents to autonomously explore the real Web, discover and connect relevant evidence from multiple independent sources through Web search, browser interaction, and evidence processing, and ultimately determine a unique factual answer. Building on this task formulation, we construct OpenDS-World, a benchmark comprising 200 challenging tasks spanning diverse information modalities, heterogeneous file formats, and interactive access requirements, with independent human verification to ensure evidence validity and answer uniqueness. We evaluate 12 frontier models under a unified tool environment and execution protocol. The best-performing model achieves 39.0% accuracy, while human evaluation across 1,000 independent attempts yields 21.1% accuracy. Further analyses of tool usage, search cost, termination behavior, and failure recovery reveal substantial differences in research strategies across models, as well as persistent challenges in tool coordination and long-horizon search management. OpenDS-World provides a unified evaluation platform for systematically assessing and advancing agents' autonomous deep search capabilities in real-world open Web environments.

Title: Uber brings ChatGPT Work to all employees with OpenAI

Text:
Uber is rolling out ChatGPT Work to more than 30,000 employees, helping teams research, analyze data, create presentations, and complete complex workflows.

Article text (excerpt):
Uber announced the company-wide rollout of ChatGPT Work , an agent that helps employees take on a wide range of tasks within ChatGPT Enterprise, starting today. The rollout will make ChatGPT Work available to more than 30,000 employees across Uber’s global workforce.
Expanding from an initial pilot of 1,000 employees, the rollout will give teams across Uber access to an agentic platform designed to take on complex, multi-step tasks and deliver finished work. The expansion makes ChatGPT Work Uber’s first company-wide deployment of an agentic platform tailored for knowledge work.
ChatGPT Work connects with tools companies like Uber use on a daily basis, including Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, and Slack, enabling workers to research information, prepare meeting briefs, create presentations, analyze data and complete workflows across applications.
ChatGPT Work also gives Uber access to OpenAI’s portfolio of frontier models. Uber will benefit from models like GPT‑6.1 Sol ⁠ which will be deployed as the default capability within ChatGPT Work, balancing frontier performance and cost efficiency. Uber teams will also be supported by OpenAI multimodal capabilities, including voice and image generation, giving them the flexibility to choose the right models and tools for different needs.
The rollout will be supported by Uber’s internal AI skills library, approved integrations and dedicated employee training, helping teams across functions including operations, finance, marketing and product put the technology to work. Uber’s developers and software engineering teams will also continue using Codex to accelerate software development and streamline coding workflows.
The expansion marks another step in Uber’s broader AI strategy and its collaboration with OpenAI. The companies plan to share further insights into adoption, use cases and measurable outcomes as the rollout progresses.

Coverage from Adgully: "Uber rolls out OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work to all 30,000 global employees"
Uber has rolled out ChatGPT Work, OpenAI’s enterprise AI agent, to its global workforce of more than 30,000 employees. The companies announced the expansion on October 22, following a pilot with 1,000 employees. It is Uber’s first company-wide deployment of an agentic platform for knowledge work.
ChatGPT Work is an agent within ChatGPT Enterprise that helps employees take on a wide range of tasks and deliver finished work. It connects with tools Uber staff use every day, including Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar and Slack. Teams across operations, finance, marketing and product can use it to research information, prepare meeting briefs, create presentations, analyse data and complete workflows across applications.
GPT-6.1 Sol will be the default model within ChatGPT Work, which OpenAI says balances frontier performance and cost efficiency. Uber’s developers and software engineering teams will continue to use Codex for software development and coding workflows. The rollout will be supported by Uber’s internal AI skills library, approved integrations and dedicated employee training.
About 80 per cent of the early users in the pilot were non-engineers, Uber’s VP of engineering Sumanth Sukumar told TechCrunch. Uber said it will track how employees use the tool and what workflows they build and use the findings to guide how it deploys AI across the business. Uber did not disclose the cost of the rollout.
Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga said in the announcement that Uber wants to give everyone the tools to innovate and shape its future, calling the rollout “an exciting step toward that ambition”. OpenAI president Greg Brockman said teams across Uber can now tap OpenAI’s frontier models and agents to take on more complex work, connect the tools they use every day and get more done.
The companies said they plan to share further insights on adoption, use cases and measurable outcomes as the rollout progresses.

Background (AI agent, Wikipedia):
An AI agent is an artificial intelligence program that can make decisions, pursue goals, and take actions independently of human programmers. Agentic AI contrasts with tool-like AI use for narrow, specific tasks such as answering questions - as with chatbots in the non-agentic forms that were common in 2023, or with traditional machine learning algorithms.

Background (Foundation model, Wikipedia):
In artificial intelligence, a foundation model (FM), also known as large x model, is a machine learning or deep learning model trained on vast datasets so that it can be applied across a wide range of use cases. Generative AI applications like large language models (LLMs) are common examples of foundation models.

text:
30,000 employees just received access to an AI agent.

In the initial pilot, 80 percent of early users were non-engineers.

Here is why that ratio matters.

Uber expanded OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work across its entire global workforce.

The rollout grew from a 1,000-person test group to more than 30,000 workers.

The software connects directly to daily work tools:
• Gmail and Google Calendar
• Google Drive files
• Slack channels

Instead of answering simple questions, the system handles multi-step knowledge tasks. It prepares meeting briefs, builds slide decks, and analyzes data across applications.

Uber’s software engineers still use Codex for programming. This deployment was built for everyone else, supported by an internal skills library and dedicated employee training across operations, finance, marketing, and product.

Default operations run on GPT-6.1 Sol, a model chosen to balance frontier performance with cost efficiency.

My read: enterprise AI has crossed the line from developer tool to general office infrastructure. When four out of five early adopters do non-technical work, software deployment is no longer about generating code faster.

The catch is proven return on investment. Uber has not disclosed the cost of the deployment, and tracking employee-built workflows is only beginning.

How many multi-step tasks in your weekly routine could an agent finish without you?

Source: OpenAI, with reporting from Tech Times on MSN and Seeking Alpha
